title: Now is the time
hook: listen, friends: now is the time to serve the holy and earn the Name (Gauri Purbi M5, ang 13)
tomorrow: A wedding song at a funeral

segments.voice: Yesterday, benti, a humble request; your line was karau benantee. Today, what the request actually is.

A caravan halts at a market town. For a few days there's buying and selling, haggling and loading, and then the caravan moves on. Everyone knows the rule: what you earn here is what you carry home. Spend the market days sleeping, gambling or arguing, and you go home with empty bags. When the last hymn of Sohila explains its urgent request, it reaches for that language: profit, earning, buying, a short stay.
screen: `A MARKET TOWN, A SHORT STAY.` → `WHAT YOU EARN, YOU CARRY HOME.` → `THE HYMN SPEAKS LIKE A TRADER.`

segments.voice: Here's the request, in paraphrase. Listen, my friends: this is the time to serve the holy. Earn the profit of God here, and your dwelling hereafter will be easy. The word for profit is laahaa, an ordinary trader's word, the gain at the end of the day. Then the urgency. In paraphrase again: day and night, life is running down; O mind, meet the Guru and set your affairs in order. Anyone with a deadline understands that: the hours go whether you use them or not. The hymn goes on: this world is caught in corruption and doubt; the one who knows God crosses over. Buy what you came here to buy. Through the Guru, God comes to dwell in the mind, and you reach your own true home in ease, with no more coming and going. Then the very last request in all of Sohila. In paraphrase: Nanak, Your servant, begs for this happiness: make me the dust of the feet of the holy. So the night prayer ends on humility, the lowest place in the room, chosen on purpose. Here's why it belongs at bedtime. Night is when you count the day. What did I earn? Not money: kindness, attention, remembering. The hymn doesn't scold. It just says the market's still open. Now is the time.
screen: `LAAHAA: THE DAY'S PROFIT.` · `DAY AND NIGHT, LIFE RUNS DOWN.` · `BUY WHAT YOU CAME TO BUY.` · `MAKE ME THE DUST OF THE HOLY'S FEET.` · then, large: `NOW IS THE TIME.`

segments.voice: Let one person come to mind, someone at home, someone you owe a thank-you, and one small kindness you could give them tonight: a filled water glass, a note, three warm words, a dish washed that isn't yours. Picture yourself giving it, and let that be the day's profit. If you pray, say Waheguru once.
Seva, selfless service: Guru Arjan's request in Sohila's last hymn: listen, friends, life is running down day and night, so serve the holy and earn the profit of the Name today.
Your line: what did I earn today. A trader's question, asked kindly. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Sikhs recite this hymn as the last of Kirtan Sohila every night, so its call that now is the time to serve and remember is often the final teaching heard before sleep.

chat.who: a friend who works long hours
chat.says: Why does Sohila's last hymn talk about profit and buying, like a trader?
options: Life runs down day and night, so now is the time to serve and earn the Name's lasting profit.
It's business advice: work hard by day so you can rest easy at night.
It says the real profit comes later, so there's no hurry to serve or remember now.
